question: Why did an airport etch a fly into its urinals?
answer: To give men something to aim at. At Amsterdam's Schiphol airport the little fly was said to cut spillage by 80%. Thaler and Sunstein use it as the model nudge: cheap, easy to ignore, no rules or fines, and yet it changes what most people do.
move: A good nudge makes the right thing easy and leaves you free to ignore it.
simply: Give people a target and they aim for it. Nobody needs a sign saying 'please aim'.
why: Small design changes often beat rules and lectures, at home, at work or in public policy.
source: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein, Nudge, 2008
reference: Richard H. Thaler and Cass R. Sunstein, Nudge (Yale University Press, 2008), introduction
